items.text: ALL nodes are `step` type (fresh context each time, no conversation history)
items.reasoning: The comment uses the old engine's naming; the YAML uses `task`, which is the stateless kind today (semantics §1.1). Isolated nodes that depend on earlier work are FC004's job, which is not implemented yet.

items.text: NO `save_as` variables — nothing is passed between steps
items.reasoning: No step reads a variable, so there is nothing undefined for FC001-FC003 to report. The problem is that steps refer to earlier work without receiving it (FC004, not yet implemented).

items.text: NO retry loop — if fix fails, no way to go back
items.reasoning: A missing recovery path is a property of the goal (fix verified before submit), not of information flow. Lean4Agent checks it with sub-goal annotations; FlowCheck has no notion of goals.

items.text: Each step must re-explore the codebase from scratch
items.reasoning: Consequence of items 1-2; FC004 territory (not yet implemented).

items.text: verify_fix has NO info about what implement_fix actually changed
items.reasoning: verify_fix is a task with no upstream input; whether its instruction refers to the fix is what FC004 checks (not yet implemented).

extra_findings.note: Not in Lean4Agent's list: the condition uses `contains`, which AgentSPEX's condition grammar does not support, so it is always false and reproduction_retry never runs.

items.text: The terminal `create_and_submit_patch` step reads NOTHING upstream
items.reasoning: A task with no upstream reads is not an undefined read; FC004 (not yet implemented) is the rule that targets it.

items.text: The `for_each` probe_edge_case body has NO save_as — per-edge-case findings evaporate
items.reasoning: Visible from the YAML (an LLM step in a loop body whose output is never saved), but FlowCheck only checks reads, not outputs that are produced and dropped. A "discarded output" rule would cover it.

items.text: `reproduction_retry` overwrites repro_report in the then-branch but the else-branch writes nothing
items.reasoning: repro_report is defined on both paths (written before the `if`), so there is no undefined read; Lean4Agent itself notes both branches leave it non-empty. Whether the two states mean the same thing needs postconditions. Separately, FlowCheck finds that this `if` can never take the then-branch at all (FC005, see extra_findings).

extra_findings.note: Not in Lean4Agent's list: `switch: on:` is parsed by YAML 1.1 as the boolean key True, so the switch has no `variable` and always runs the default branch; the four strategy-specific fix steps can never run.
Not in Lean4Agent's list: `contains` is unsupported, so adjust_fix_once never runs.

items.text: `for_each` body step `inspect_candidate` has NO save_as — scouting results are lost
items.reasoning: Same as swe/failed_workflow_2 item 2: discarded outputs are not checked.

items.text: `adjust_fix_once` runs exactly once and flows straight into edge_case_plan WITHOUT a second verify step
items.reasoning: A missing verification step is a goal-coverage property, not information flow.
The variable is defined; that it no longer describes the code after the adjustment is a semantic fact about what the steps do, which needs postconditions.

items.text: All LLM nodes are `step` (fresh context each time) — no implicit retry via conversation history
items.reasoning: Old-engine naming; the YAML uses `task`. Isolation is FC004's job (not yet implemented).

extra_findings.note: option_judgment is only written inside the recheck `while`, which FlowCheck must assume may run zero times. Here it always runs (recheck_count starts at 0 < 3), so this is a path-sensitivity false positive that phase two should discharge.

items.text: Evidence is NOT grounded: keyword_hits → opaque evidence_snippets buffer; no grounding/verification node
items.reasoning: Whether evidence is verbatim and verified is a property of step outputs (boundedEvidenceList / verbatimSubstring predicates), not of which variables exist.

items.text: Fragmented judgement: four independent evaluate_A..D over evidence_snippets
items.reasoning: A design property checked through goal coverage in Lean4Agent.

items.text: infoSound = FALSE: evaluate_A..D require evidence_snippets, which no semantic node produces
items.reasoning: At the variable level evidence_snippets is defined: a set_variable initialises it before the loop and the loop appends to it. Lean4Agent's information model doesn't count set_variable as a producer of an information atom. That distinction needs its annotations; FlowCheck correctly reports no undefined read here.

items.text: search_keyword_in_paper is BROKEN: save_as = None and it reads a `{{keyword}}` loop variable never bound by a producing node
items.reasoning: FlowCheck finds the step broken for a different, concrete reason. `keyword` *is* bound (it is the for_each variable), but the loop is `in: question_analysis.keywords`, which AgentSPEX looks up as one flat key (control.py:167-169). So the loop runs once with keyword = "question_analysis.keywords". The missing save_as (results dropped) is not checked by FlowCheck (see swe/failed_workflow_2 item 2).

elaip/failed_workflow_3.stale: The YAML was rewritten in Lean4Agent commit 17b2099 after the IR and this Lean file were written (see the cross-check, category IR-stale-vs-YAML). The documented problem names steps and variables (recheck_summary, option_judgment) that no longer exist in the YAML.

extra_findings.note: combined_judgment is only written inside the recheck while loop; same pattern as elaip/failed_workflow_1.

items.text: NO consolidated verdict-validated option_judgment; finalize blocks on the missing option_judgment atom
items.reasoning: A validated, consolidated verdict is an output-quality property. In the current YAML the finaliser reads combined_judgment, which exists on every path except a zero-iteration recheck loop (FC002, a path-sensitivity false positive like elaip/failed_workflow_1's).

passed_findings.reasoning: fix_description is only written inside `while fix_attempt < max_fix_attempts`. The loop always runs at least once, because fix_attempt is set to 0 just before it and max_fix_attempts is 3; the Lean4Agent IR records loop_executes_at_least_once: true. FlowCheck is path-insensitive and must assume zero iterations. Phase two's feasibility oracle would discharge this.

A real bug that Lean4Agent passes. AgentSPEX looks up for_each `in` as one flat key (control.py:167-169), so `in: question_keywords.keywords` iterates once over the literal string "question_keywords.keywords", and search_paper_for_keyword searches for that string instead of the extracted keywords. Lean4Agent's IR builder records only the branch_path "for_each:keyword" and never models `in`, so it can't see this.

categories.IR-linearised-edges: The ELAIP IR builder links each flattened node to the next one only (experiments/elaip_LeanEvolve/build_layer2_ir.py:394-399), so it has no loop-back, loop-skip or branch edges, and it chains the last node of one branch to the first node of the next. FlowCheck models the real control flow.
categories.IR-instruction-only-reads: The ELAIP IR builder takes reads from `instruction` only and records none for set_variable (build_layer2_ir.py:243, 292). AgentSPEX template-expands set_variable `value` (variables.py:92), so FlowCheck counts those reads.
categories.IR-stale-vs-YAML: The YAML was changed after the IR was generated (ELAIP failed_workflow_3: rewritten in Lean4Agent commit 17b2099; SWE failed_workflow_2: the old `discover` step was ported to a task named `edge_case_list`, see the comment at failed_workflow_2.yaml:229). The IR describes the older workflow.
categories.IR-abstraction: The SWE IR is a hand/LLM-authored abstraction: it omits scaffolding steps (set_variable, increment), merges or drops some LLM steps and an inner `if`, models for_each as whileLoop, and leaves out some templated reads. FlowCheck lists every step and every `{{...}}` the runtime expands.
categories.IR-conceptual-read: The IR lists a read that the YAML never template-expands: the variable is only named in prose (e.g. 'Source: candidate_files_report', 'the PR description', a path mentioned in text). At runtime the value is not substituted, so FlowCheck has no read. (Several of these are exactly what FC004 is meant to flag.)
categories.IR-conceptual-write: The IR lists a write, but the YAML step has no save_as, so nothing is written at runtime.
categories.IR-runtime-ignores: The IR lists the read a broken construct was meant to perform, but AgentSPEX never performs it: the condition uses the unsupported `contains` operator (always false, conditions.py:142-206), or the switch has no `variable` key because YAML parsed `on:` as a boolean (control.py:405-417). FlowCheck reports these as FC005 instead.
categories.IR-type-label: The IR labels the step with a different step type than the YAML uses.
